paraphrase: By alternately breathing through iḍā and piṅgalā while meditating on the discs of sun and moon, the channels of the restrained one become pure; from purification of the channels come holding the breath at will, kindling of the fire, manifestation of the inner sound (nāda) and health.

paraphrase: How can yogīs succeed who do not know in their own body the six centres, the sixteen supports, the three aims and the five voids — who do not know their own body as a house of one pillar and nine doors with five presiding deities?

paraphrase: Homage to Śrī Mīnanātha, the yogī praised through ages and aeons for holding the lamp-flame of the self motionless by the root lock and other means, in whom Ādinātha himself became a great ocean of the fragrance of knowledge.

paraphrase: The breath goes out with the sound 'ha' and enters again with 'sa'; the jīva always repeats this mantra 'haṃsa haṃsa', twenty-one thousand six hundred times in a day and night; this is the gāyatrī called ajapā, which gives yogins liberation; by merely resolving on it one is freed from all sins; there is no knowledge, repetition or wisdom equal to it; this gāyatrī arises from kuṇḍalinī and sustains life — the one who knows this science of the breath knows yoga.
